t: This is the site of Sir Walter St John's Grammar School for Boys, in Battersea. The school was known to generations of pupils as Sinjuns. It was founded by Sir Walter St John, the third baronet, who was an English politician and lived from 1622 to 1708. As the population and the English educational system changed, so did the school, and it finally closed in 1986 to 1987. The name above the door still points back to its founder.
